cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: <important if="you are running tests or typechecks">
cards.claim: The repo's own agent file wraps task-specific rules in <important if="condition"> blocks (about 12 of them) so only matching rules carry weight, which is the CLAUDE.md-trimming technique applied to its own file.
cards.evidence_detail: Used in practice in the repo's own AGENTS.md; no adherence numbers.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md: wrap the Commands, Build traps and Invariants sections in conditional blocks instead of deleting them
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md covers the idea, not this file

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: you must NEVER pipe the output of test commands to head/tail/grep/etc
cards.claim: Tell the agent to run the full test command once and filter the spooled output file afterwards, so long-running tests are never re-run just to change a grep.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule in the repo's agent file; relies on the Bash tool's persisted-output spooling.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md commands section / phase routine verification step

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Do not pipe test, typecheck, or quality output to head/tail/grep/etc.
cards.claim: A PreToolUse Bash hook regex-detects test, typecheck and lint commands piped into head/tail/grep and exits 2 with an explanation, turning the prose rule R40-2 into an enforced one.
cards.evidence_detail: Working hook script (about 40 lines of bash plus a node JSON parse); no metrics.
cards.landing: Hooks (a harness review skipped hooks; this re-opens it): a hook on the verification commands

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Typecheck and quality checks are failing due to an ongoing merge.
cards.claim: A Stop hook runs prebuild, quality and typecheck and exits 2 on failure so the agent cannot finish with a red tree, but skips the checks while .git/MERGE_HEAD exists and tells the agent to continue the merge instead.
cards.evidence_detail: Working script; the merge-in-progress exemption shows a failure mode they hit.
cards.landing: Hooks (re-opens a skipped item): a Stop-hook gate that runs the same checks as CI

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: "MAX_THINKING_TOKENS": 32000
cards.claim: The committed project settings set MAX_THINKING_TOKENS to 32000 and CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR to 1, and allow-list only the spec_metadata.sh script.
cards.evidence_detail: Three lines in a committed settings file; no rationale given.
cards.landing: .claude/settings.json env block

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: "spec needed", "research needed", "research in progress", "research in review", "ready for plan"
cards.claim: Workflow phase is externalised as a ticket status ladder (spec needed through code review) that the agent sets through a CLI, so phase state is visible outside the transcript.
cards.evidence_detail: Status names listed in the agent file; used by the product's own workflow.
cards.landing: Phase routine: state ladder on the draft PR (labels) so skipped phases show from outside

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The `Grep` and `Glob` and `Search` tools WILL NOT WORK. They do not traverse symlinks.
cards.claim: Task artifacts live in a symlinked .humanlayer/tasks/<slug> folder outside the code repo, so the agent must use ls and is told never to commit them; Glob and Grep silently miss symlinked directories.
cards.evidence_detail: Repeated in three skill files (create-plan, implement-plan, AGENTS.md); a trap they hit.
cards.landing: Knowledge-store design: do not store agent notes behind symlinks; a trap list for the evidence folders

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Never stop another worktree's stack, its tmux session, or the shared Caddy
cards.claim: Each worktree gets its own containers and ports via a devstack, created by a script that takes the ticket id plus two words, with an explicit rule never to stop another worktree's stack because another agent may be using it.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule written after parallel-agent collisions; no numbers.
cards.landing: Phase routine (one phase per new chat): a worktree-isolation rule when several agents run in parallel

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: do not use git commit --amend unless the user expressly requested it
cards.claim: Fix-ups and follow-ons are made as new commits, never amends, unless the user asks.
cards.evidence_detail: One conditional rule in the agent file.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md or PR review checklist (head SHA stays traceable)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: to add values to .env, don't read it, use echo "KEY=VALUE" >> .env
cards.claim: The agent is told to append to the env file without reading it, keeping secrets out of context, and to consider updating .env.example.
cards.evidence_detail: One conditional rule.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md security invariants

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: This rule overrides direct test commands in plans, outlines, and tickets.
cards.claim: Packages whose tests need containers must be run only through one root script that starts and tears down the services, and the agent file explicitly outranks commands written in plans.
cards.evidence_detail: Precedence rule in the agent file, aimed at stale commands in generated plans.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md precedence statement; plan template validation block

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: oxlint intentionally emits thousands of `no-explicit-any` / `no-non-null-assertion`
cards.claim: The default check scripts run linters in quiet mode inside the silent wrapper so only failures print, and the verbose command is documented as something to avoid because warnings flood the context window.
cards.evidence_detail: Describes thousands of warnings; no token counts.
cards.landing: Backpressure scripts: a quiet default for lint and test commands in CLAUDE.md
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Context-Efficient Backpressure names hack/run_silent.sh but not this repo state

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Run command silently, show output only on failure
cards.claim: The backpressure wrapper writes command output to a temp file, prints one tick line on success and the full output only on failure, with a VERBOSE=1 escape hatch.
cards.evidence_detail: About 150 lines of bash; the script has moved from hack/ to scripts/.
cards.landing: scripts/ wrapper around pytest, ruff, mypy, npm test in CLAUDE.md commands

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The task sidebar hides toggles by omitting change handlers, not by disabling switches.
cards.claim: A .agents/context-shards/ folder holds one short design note per subsystem (components, flow diagram, transition table, 'Important Gotchas' list) that an agent reads on demand instead of loading it through CLAUDE.md.
cards.evidence_detail: One shard read, about 60 lines; tied to the 'Context Shards' early-access feature in release 0.164.0.
cards.landing: Knowledge-store design: per-subsystem shards with a Gotchas list, referenced from a thin CLAUDE.md
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) release notes name 'Context Shards' early access only

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Before launching, the engine checks for an existing session with the destination dedup label
cards.claim: Workflow phase hand-off is a transition table (flag, source label, destination, skill) with a dedup label per destination, so a session that reaches ready-for-input can launch the next phase exactly once.
cards.evidence_detail: Describes product code, five transitions from research questions to PR description.
cards.landing: Phase routine as a table (phase, completion artifact, next phase) that a script or reviewer can check

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: All non-trivial operations should be delegated to sub-agents.
cards.claim: An orchestrator skill tells the main agent to delegate research to locator/analyzer/pattern sub-agents and noisy bash (aws, gh, logs) to bash sub-agents, launching parallel agents only when tasks do not overlap.
cards.evidence_detail: Ten-line skill; no results given.
cards.landing: Skill under .claude/skills/ plus more custom agents beyond the Haiku locator

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Spawn sub-agents to verify each claim is still accurate
cards.claim: An autonomous second pass on a research doc finds thin sections, fills gaps with sub-agents, then re-verifies every file-path, line and behaviour claim by sub-agent and corrects the doc, splitting any document over 1000 lines.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill text; same doc structure as the research phase, with 'document, do not critique' rules.
cards.landing: Verifier step for the knowledge store: claim-by-claim re-verification of a diagnosis before it is filed

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: DO NOT read ticket files - research must stay objective about the current codebase.
cards.claim: Research is kept objective by withholding the ticket and the desired change: the research agent gets only neutral current-state questions, and the request lives in a separate document.
cards.evidence_detail: Repeated in grind-research, create-research-questions and the plan skill ('DO NOT read research questions documents').
cards.landing: Cold-resume trial and the refuter pass (fresh agents see only the artifact, not the ask); knowledge-store entries as ticket-free facts
cards.inventory_ref: (B) Mar 2026 RPI retrospective covers research-prompt opinions, not this input-withholding rule

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Asking multiple questions at once is bewildering.
cards.claim: A grill-me skill interviews the owner one question at a time down each branch of the design tree, with a recommended answer for each, and explores the codebase instead of asking whenever the code can answer.
cards.evidence_detail: Seven-line skill.
cards.landing: Skill for the owner decision gates (plan approval, P0a questions)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Use these terms exactly - don't substitute "component," "service," "API," or "boundary."
cards.claim: A shared vocabulary skill (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) pins design terms so agents and humans use the same words; a deep module is a lot of behaviour behind a small interface.
cards.evidence_detail: First 60 lines read; terms come from Ousterhout and Feathers.
cards.landing: Skill backing the import-boundary contracts and slice rules

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: keep your prompt short, do not duplicate details that are already in the plan
cards.claim: The implementation skill is an orchestrator that launches one implementer sub-agent per plan phase with a one-line prompt pointing at the plan, re-runs automated checks itself, waits for human sign-off, then commits and resumes from the first unchecked box.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill text; implementer agent is separate and 'stops after automated verification'.
cards.landing: Phase routine: orchestrator re-runs checks itself rather than trusting the implementer's report; checkbox plan as resume state

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: plan > structure outline > design discussion > research > ticket
cards.claim: When workflow documents conflict, the most recent one wins, with a fixed precedence order, and documents carry chronological NN- prefixes found by listing the folder.
cards.evidence_detail: Explicit precedence rule in the plan skill.
cards.landing: Ship-plan §0 precedence rule between plan, CLAUDE.md and decisions journal

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Not every phase requires manual validation, don't put steps for manual validation just to have them.
cards.claim: Each plan phase must be independently testable with runnable automated checks and only specific, actionable manual steps where needed.
cards.evidence_detail: Plan-writing guideline.
cards.landing: Plan template: per-phase automated verification commands

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Users run each phase in a separate context window by default.
cards.claim: Portable RPI is one entry skill that routes to per-step process files, picks or reuses a task directory by branch name, numbers documents, stamps frontmatter with repos and SHAs, and suggests the next command naming the task directory so each phase can start in a fresh session.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill text from the October 2026 portability commits; version 1.1.0.
cards.landing: Phase routine hand-off: every phase ends by printing the exact next-session command and the artifact path with repo SHAs
cards.inventory_ref: (B) Oct 2026 / Nov 2026 humanlayer/skills commits (commit titles only)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Make it shorter, more visual, and easier for a person to digest
cards.claim: After writing any workflow document the agent re-reads a prose-style reference and a show-me reference and cuts words and sections that do not earn their place, replacing dense prose with the smallest visual that makes the point.
cards.evidence_detail: Added in the 2026-10-31 'prose reference and a document review step' commit.
cards.landing: A review step on CLAUDE.md and phase-closing messages (length pass) and the one-page owner view
cards.inventory_ref: (B) Nov 2026 lists the commit title only

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The RPI framework authors recommend not committing the artifacts.
cards.claim: Workflow artifacts go in .agents/artifacts/<branch> and are not committed, which differs from FixFlow keeping evidence folders with sha256 manifests in the repo.
cards.evidence_detail: One sentence in the skill.
cards.landing: Decision on whether program evidence belongs in git (a counter-position to note)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Keep this pass small; the next research session does the full investigation.
cards.claim: A research-questions phase drafts two to seven neutral, current-state questions with concrete path pointers, and saves the original request in a separate numbered file so later design and implementation sessions can find the desired result.
cards.evidence_detail: Process file added in the Oct 2026 portable RPI work (the Q in QRSPI).
cards.landing: Cold-resume trial design: question file separate from the request; a diagnosis phase input

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: this context may or may not be relevant to your tasks.
cards.claim: Claude Code's system reminder tells the model CLAUDE.md may be irrelevant, so the more of it that does not apply to the task, the more of it gets ignored; the cure is conditional blocks plus cutting.
cards.evidence_detail: Mechanism quoted from the Claude Code system reminder; no experiment in the skill.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim: remove or wrap sections not relevant to most tasks
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md (repo humanlayer/skills, plugin improve-claude-md)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Frontier models can reliably follow a few hundred.
cards.claim: Instruction budget heuristic: models follow a few hundred instructions, Claude Code's own prompt already uses about 50, so CLAUDE.md must be as lean as possible.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as fact; no source or benchmark given.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md length target (the 390-line file against this budget)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Cut any instruction that a linter, formatter, or pre-commit hook can enforce
cards.claim: Delete from CLAUDE.md anything a linter, formatter or hook enforces, anything discoverable from existing code patterns, code snippets (use file paths) and vague advice; keep all commands; leave a rule bare only if it applies to 90%+ of tasks.
cards.evidence_detail: Numbered principles in the skill (rule of thumb 90%).
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim rules; also pushes enforceable rules toward a pre-commit gate or hooks (both skipped by the review)

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Do not shard into separate files that require the agent to make tool calls
cards.claim: Prefer inline conditional blocks over splitting CLAUDE.md into extra files, unless the extra context is very long, because discovery by tool call is itself unreliable.
cards.evidence_detail: Principle 3 in the skill.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim: weigh against the knowledge-store pilot's sharding approach (tension with R40-14)

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Recommended: Yes, bound to 1 open PR per agent loop.
cards.claim: Scheduled agent loops no-op when an open PR carrying the loop's label already exists, so agent output cannot pile up faster than humans review it; manual dispatch bypasses the bound; a memory file carries standing feedback between runs.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill text; review-fatigue example of 5+ unreviewed PRs a week, not measured.
cards.landing: Workflow library: a saved scheduled-loop template with PR bound and agent-memory file
cards.inventory_ref: (B) Jun 2026 lists design-control-loop only as a commit

cards.author: Kyle
cards.quote: Make each component runnable locally and standalone before wiring it into CI
cards.claim: Design an agentic loop as set point, sensor, controller, actuator and optional dampener (a regression gate); build sensor and controller as local scripts first, then wire the scheduled workflow, with a human on the loop.
cards.evidence_detail: Control-theory framing in the skill; one worked example reference.
cards.landing: Workflow library entry: sensor-script-then-agent pattern; regression gate for slice-boundary violations
cards.inventory_ref: (B) Jun 2026 design-control-loop skill added by Kyle

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: log-based state, tool support, hook support, subagents and skill facades, event streaming, auto-compaction
cards.claim: Fold's core keeps session state as an event log (resume from the log, a conflicting session id fails rather than starting a new session) and exposes auto-compaction as a single flag, autoCompact enabled; the README has no section describing compaction, sub-agent or RLM-like orchestration behaviour.
cards.evidence_detail: 95-line README; the three named features are one-line mentions only, so the grep found nothing deeper to read.
cards.landing: Nowhere obvious; log-as-state and fail-on-conflicting-identity echo cold-resume from the repository

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Claude gets `write`/`edit`, while GPT/Codex gets `apply_patch`.
cards.claim: The tool set advertised to the model is chosen per model on every request, since each model family is trained on a different edit tool.
cards.evidence_detail: Design statement in the README.
cards.landing: Effort/model routing: harness choices per model family

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Network errors and 408, 425, 429, 502, 503 and 504 retry forever
cards.claim: The mirroring queue retries ambiguous failures forever with 0.5 s doubling to 30 s, retries a 500 five times then skips, skips 400/413/422, pauses on 401 after one token refresh, and drops the oldest events at 5000 items or 50 MB but never status updates.
cards.evidence_detail: Documented policy with exact codes and caps.
cards.landing: Echoes FixFlow's outbox classification (kept vs failed); a reference table for retry classes

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Event ids are fixed, so resends don't make copies.
cards.claim: Resume after a crash works from a binding file holding the last acked entry plus fixed event ids, so a restarted session resends everything after it without duplicates, and exit flushes within a fixed 5 s budget.
cards.evidence_detail: Documented design with binding file layout.
cards.landing: Resume-from-server-truth principle; cold-resume trial design (acked pointer plus idempotent ids)

cards.source_title: humanlayer-pi README.md (What it sends / does not send)
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The extension reads it at load and deletes it from pi's environment
cards.claim: The extension removes its access token from the process environment at load so the model and tools never see it, and limits the diff to exclude .env files, but admits there is no redaction of prompts or file contents.
cards.evidence_detail: Documented behaviour and an explicit 'no redaction' limit.
cards.landing: Secrets handling note for agent sessions that mirror transcripts

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: to look there first when asked to continue a task
cards.claim: Every prompt appends a system-prompt section giving the task folder path, saying files written there reach the task and to look there first when continuing, so the session's memory is a folder the harness syncs, not the transcript.
cards.evidence_detail: Describes injected text; the folder is added to .git/info/exclude, never .gitignore.
cards.landing: Knowledge-store/cold-resume: a per-prompt pointer to the store; it also makes consultation observable server-side

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The tests use Node's own test runner, a faux model and an in-process mock cloud
cards.claim: The extension is tested without network or API keys by a faux model plus a mock cloud with injectable failures (route, status, times, hang, network drop), so retry paths are exercised deterministically.
cards.evidence_detail: Mock cloud described with a fail-rule API; tests run in CI without keys.
cards.landing: Verifier tooling: fault-injection mock for the outbox and dispatcher tests

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Calls in one session run one at a time, in order
cards.claim: Tool calls for comment threads are serialised per session because a reply reopens a thread that a resolve in the same turn closed, an ordering hazard similar to the outbox race FixFlow documents.
cards.evidence_detail: One sentence rationale.
cards.landing: Reference for the known outbox mutual-exclusion defect

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: It refuses while the plugin, the pi skills or `packages/` have uncommitted changes.
cards.claim: The publish script builds from the source repo, commits 'Sync from synclayer@<sha>' to the install repo, and refuses on uncommitted changes, so every published copy names the source commit it came from.
cards.evidence_detail: Release procedure in README.
cards.landing: Workflow library publishing: stamp saved workflows or skills with the source SHA and refuse a dirty tree

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: CONTRIBUTING.md lists every check a pull request must pass.
cards.claim: The root README is human onboarding only, points to CONTRIBUTING for the PR checks, and keeps agent instructions in a separate AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md is a byte-identical copy) with human-only setup in HUMANS.md.
cards.evidence_detail: File layout of the repo: README, HUMANS.md, AGENTS.md identical to CLAUDE.md.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md split: audience-specific files and a single source for the agent file

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Run `./scripts/setup-agent-browser.sh` to generate an encryption key
cards.claim: One-time human setup lives in a file addressed to humans, with an encryption key for the agent-browser session store so agents reuse an authenticated browser profile without logging in.
cards.evidence_detail: Eleven-line file; AGENTS.md says to run agent-browser with a saved profile and switch to headed only for login.
cards.landing: Verification of the web manager with a saved browser profile (agent-browser skill)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: use the HumanLayer library researcher tool
cards.claim: Up-to-date library documentation is fetched through a dedicated researcher tool (a sub-agent behind an MCP tool) rather than by the main agent browsing.
cards.evidence_detail: One rule; the same tool is shipped in the pi and opencode plugins.
cards.landing: Custom agent for library documentation lookups beside the Haiku locator

gaps: Only 4 of about 25 skills in humanlayer/humanlayer/.claude/skills were read (subagent-orchestrator, grind-research, grill-me, head of codebase-design); the other skills (calldiff, no-use-effect, test-it-locally, grind-design-discussion, react-doctor, etc.) were not read.
Only create-plan and implement-plan of the 22 skills in apps/riptide-rpi-claude-plugin/skills were read; no implementer-agent definition or describe-pr skill read.
apps/riptide-daemon docs, docs/ guide (apps/docs/guide/skills-workflows.md) and CONTRIBUTING.md not read; no thoughts/ folder exists in the tree (task artifacts are symlinked outside it).
humanlayer/fold has no README sections on compaction, sub-agents or RLM-like orchestration (single-line mentions only); source code under packages/ not read.
improve-claude-md, build-iterated-agentic-loop and design-control-loop were read only to about 5000-6000 bytes; their references/ files were not read.
humanlayer/skills commit messages were read as titles only; diffs of the Oct 2026 portable-RPI commits, the prose.md reference and the visual-pr skill were not read.
scripts/run_silent.sh was read to about line 60 of about 150; the Makefile use was not checked.

Authorship in the monorepo files cannot be separated between Dex and teammates; cards use 'Dex+others' except skills committed by dexhorthy (Dex) and Kyle-added loop skills (Kyle, inferred from the inventory).
